claims.text: The deviation is established on this trip's own trace, and the trace is the field that governs. EV-GPS-02833 records trace_distance_km of 23.22 km between the recorded pickup event (14:53:35) and the recorded dropoff event (15:23:45), against the booking-time optimal of 18.4 km carried on EV-TRIP-02833. That is an excess of 4.82 km, or 26.20% of optimal. Both limbs of the POL-RD-01 gate are passed: 26.20% is greater than the 20% proportional threshold, and 4.82 km is greater than the 0.8 km absolute threshold. I do not rely on the rounded convenience copy trip_record.actual_distance_km of 23.2 for this test, because POL-RD-01 expressly forbids citing it for the threshold test.

The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes, so no corroboration requirement is imported and no escalation is triggered on this ground. EV-GPS-02833 carries 182 fixes at a 10 second sample interval against a 10 second expected interval, 100.0% coverage, an empty gaps array and max_gap_sec of 0.0. None of the POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) fires: there is no gap over 90 seconds, no straight-line jump over 500 m, and no sustained interval above 30 seconds. The deviation therefore may be, and is, established on the trace alone.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged on both limbs. (a) Same trip: EV-TRIP-02833, EV-GPS-02833 and EV-FARE-02833 all carry trip_id TRP-02833, and the trip_record started_at of 2026-08-24T14:53:35+08:00 matches the gps_trace first_fix_at to the second, so the artifacts describe the same trip. (b) Excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from an unimpaired trace: 4.82 km and 26.20% on EV-GPS-02833. The burden then shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause, and the bare assertion 'Traffic.' points to neither.

The driver's traffic excuse cannot be run on this record and must be discarded. POL-RD-03 requires a traffic_advisory that names a road or segment the optimal route traverses, carries a validity window overlapping the time the trace shows the vehicle would have reached that segment, and is matched by a route leaving the corridor before and rejoining after. The only advisory artifact in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-02833-01, is MISSING: it has no payload, the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT fired, and its weight_multiplier is 0.0 — I disclose that impairment expressly under POL-GEN-02(1) and cite the artifact only for its absence. No advisory covers the Jurong Point corridor in this window, so the POL-RD-03 comparison is undecidable, the clause is unavailable, and under POL-RD-13 the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08: it neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies an amended optimal route.

The driver's uncited traffic assertion is not an escalation trigger, so the case can and should be decided with money moving. EV-ADVIS-02833-01 is named by no party in support of the excuse; the counterparty statement 'Traffic.' cites no evidence id at all. Under POL-RD-13(1) an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact within POL-RD-10(5) — the absence of an artifact no party has cited is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction in it. Every other POL-RD-10 trigger is absent too: trip identifiers match across the three artifacts, no pickup or dropoff timestamps disagree, the trace is not impaired, and the refund is well under SGD 150.00 and under charged_total. The rider should therefore receive a monetary partial refund rather than having the amount held on an escalation.

No exculpatory clause on the driver's side is available on the artifacts. EV-CHAT-02833 is COMPLETE with message_count 0 and an empty messages array, so there is no rider instruction that could exonerate any part of the excess under POL-RD-04, and the whole 4.82 km stands. The chat log is likewise the artifact POL-RD-04 and POL-RD-05 both require, so neither clause can be invoked: there is no detour request to corroborate and no waypoint_hint to test.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02 and runs as follows on the METERED fare. recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 18.4 km = 13.80 distance + 0.28 x 24.8 min = 6.944 time) x the surge_multiplier of 1.0 recorded on EV-FARE-02833, plus 0.80 platform fee, plus 0.00 ERP and tolls on the optimal route, plus 0.00 waiting time fee, less 0.00 promo discount = 25.3440. Refund = charged_total 30.46 less 25.3440 = 5.1160, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 5.15. The refund is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, so the outcome is not NO_ACTION, and it is 16.80% of charged_total, well short of the 90% that would make it a FULL_REFUND. The rider's remedy is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 5.15.

The fare carries no pass-through line that could change the figure in either direction, so SGD 5.15 is the complete rider remedy. EV-FARE-02833 shows erp_lines total 0.00, no airport surcharge, waiting_time_fee 0.00 and cancellation_fee 0.00, so there is no off-route gantry to refund as a standalone correction and equally no pass-through line to be double-counted on top of the POL-RD-02 amount — the anti-double-count rule in POL-RD-09(1) is satisfied on these figures.

One point in the claim as filed is not supported by the record, and I do not press it. The assertion that 'this driver has six deviation flags' rests on driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags on EV-DPROF-02833, which is a LIFETIME counter; POL-RD-06 asks instead for deviation_flags_90d, which on this profile is 0, and POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting the lifetime counter for the trailing-window one. There is also no PATTERN to establish and no uplift to seek: the measured excess of 26.20% is below the 50% that POL-RD-01 makes a MATERIAL deviation, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged on this trip at all, and the rider's entitlement does not depend on it. It rests on this trip's own trace under POL-RD-01 and on the POL-RD-02 arithmetic.

The rider's own profile does not add any corroboration hurdle here. POL-RD-08 imposes the extra-corroboration condition only where rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 4 or more and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1 or fewer. On EV-RPROF-02833 deviation_claims_60d is 1 — below that gate — so the condition does not apply, and in any event the clause states that the factor may never be used to deny a claim that is otherwise proven. The deviation is proven on the trace and the refund follows.

The refund on this trip is arithmetic, and it is modest. The ledger charges SGD 30.46, and the POL-RD-02 recomputation on the booked optimal route of 18.4 km and 24.8 minutes gives (3.80 + 0.75 x 18.4 + 0.28 x 24.8) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee = SGD 25.344, so the refund before rounding is SGD 5.116 and rounds UP to SGD 5.15. The fare model on the breakdown is METERED, so POL-RD-02 and not POL-RD-11 governs, and the surge multiplier was read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (1.0), not assumed.

The refund of SGD 5.15 is only 16.8% of the SGD 30.46 charged_total, nowhere near the 90% share that would substitute a FULL_REFUND for the partial under POL-RD-02. The rider's demand for a full refund of the trip is therefore unavailable on the arithmetic, and the amount pleaded (SGD 7.50) is itself above the ceiling the policy sets on this record.

On the trace that governs under POL-RD-01, the excess is 4.82 km, or 26.20% of the 18.4 km booked optimal (trace_distance_km 23.22 km; POL-RD-01 requires the trace figure and forbids citing the rounded trip_record copy of 23.2 km for the threshold test). That clears the establishment gate of 0.8 km and 20%, but it is far short of the materiality gate of more than 50% or more than 8.0 km. The deviation here is established but NOT material, so POL-RD-06(b)'s uplift to FULL_REFUND of charged_total, which is confined to a deviation that is both MATERIAL and substantiated on this trip's evidence, is never engaged.

POL-RD-06's pattern test runs on two named fields and both are on the file: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 260, a ratio of 0.000. Neither limb of the test (3 or more trailing-90-day flags, or a ratio of 0.05 or more with at least 40 completed trips) is satisfied, so no pattern is established, the balance is not resolved against the driver under POL-RD-06(a), and there is no basis for a POL-RD-06(c) referral to driver-conduct review.

The only ground the rider pleads is that 'this driver has six deviation flags'. That figure is driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags, a LIFETIME counter; it is not the trailing-90-day counter POL-RD-06 asks for, which is 0. POL-GEN-01 lists prior_deviation_flags as CONTEXT ONLY and forbids its use as a ground of decision, naming precisely this near-synonym substitution as the commonest way an adverse finding is built on reputation instead of this trip's trace. The rider's pleaded ground must be discarded on the same footing as an uncited claim, and it is a reason to scrutinise the rider's assertions closely rather than to award a full refund.

The trace is complete and unimpaired: EV-GPS-02833 carries 182 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval, 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, which is nowhere near the POL-RD-07(a) to (c) thresholds of a 90-second gap, a 500 m jump or a sustained interval above 30 seconds. The excess is therefore measured rather than interpolated: 4.82 km is the whole of it, and no further distance may be inferred across a gap that does not exist.

Nothing may be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure. The fare breakdown carries no ERP or toll line — erp_gantries is empty and the ERP total is SGD 0.00 — and no airport surcharge (the trip ENDS at Ang Mo Kio; it does not originate at an airport), no waiting-time fee and no promo discount. There is accordingly no off-route pass-through charge for a standalone POL-RD-09 correction and no unmatched gantry line for a billing-integrity finding under POL-RD-09(4); POL-RD-09(1) forbids adding any such charge a second time in any event.

The bundle holds no traffic advisory for this trip: EV-ADVIS-02833-01 is MISSING, its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT and its weight_multiplier is 0.0, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and the driver's one-word 'Traffic.' statement supplies neither an exoneration nor an amended optimal — the computation must run against the booked optimal of 18.4 km and 24.8 minutes. The same absence does not escalate the case either: under POL-RD-13 an assertion that cites no advisory identifier cannot be invoked against one, so no POL-RD-10(5) trigger fires and the matter is decided on the trace as measured.

Both parties largely agree on the facts, and the disagreement is about the remedy. The following is addressed to the rider and the driver together.

THE DEVIATION. EV-GPS-02833 is complete and unimpaired for policy purposes: 182 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval against a 10-second expected interval, 100% coverage, an empty gaps array and max_gap_sec of 0.0. None of the POL-RD-07(a)–(c) limbs fires, so no independent corroboration is required and no escalation arises on that ground; the trace decides the deviation on its own. Its trace_distance_km is 23.22 km against the booking-time optimal of 18.4 km carried on EV-TRIP-02833. The excess is 4.82 km, or 26.20% of optimal, which passes both POL-RD-01 limbs (greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20%). Per POL-RD-01 the trace figure governs and the rounded trip_record copy of 23.2 km was not used for the threshold test. The deviation is ESTABLISHED but NOT MATERIAL: 26.20% is below the 50% figure and 4.82 km is below the 8.0 km figure, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged on this trip, its FULL_REFUND uplift is unavailable, and no driver-conduct referral is produced. The driver_profile was consulted anyway: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 260 completed trips in 90 days, so no pattern exists under either limb of POL-RD-06.

THE DRIVER'S TRAFFIC EXCUSE. The driver's statement 'Traffic.' cites no evidence id. The only advisory artifact in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-02833-01, is MISSING, its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT and its weight_multiplier is 0.0, so it can carry no fact and POL-RD-03 cannot be run on this record. No other exculpatory clause is available: EV-CHAT-02833 is complete with zero messages, so POL-RD-04 has no rider instruction to test and no waypoint_hint to corroborate; no pickup or dropoff amendment is recorded (amended_optimal_distance_km is null), so POL-RD-05 cannot run; the fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-11 does not apply; and the vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply.

THE REFUND. Under POL-RD-02 on the METERED fare: recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 × 18.4 km = 13.80 distance + 0.28 × 24.8 min = 6.944 time) × the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on EV-FARE-02833, plus 0.80 platform fee, plus 0.00 ERP/tolls, plus 0.00 waiting time, less 0.00 promo discount = SGD 25.344. Refund = charged_total 30.46 − 25.344 = SGD 5.116, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 5.15. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and is 16.8% of charged_total, well short of the 90% that would substitute a FULL_REFUND. The rider's request for a full refund of the trip (SGD 7.50) is not supported by the arithmetic. The rider's pleaded ground — 'this driver has six deviation flags' — rests on driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags, a lifetime counter that POL-GEN-01 marks context only and that POL-RD-06 does not use; the trailing-window counter it does use is 0. That ground was discarded and cannot carry the claim; the rider's entitlement rests on this trip's own trace and on the POL-RD-02 arithmetic, as the rider's own submission accepts.

PASS-THROUGH LINES. EV-FARE-02833 carries no ERP or toll lines (erp_gantries empty, ERP total SGD 0.00), no airport surcharge (the trip ENDS at Ang Mo Kio and does not originate at an airport), no waiting-time fee and no promo discount. There is therefore nothing to add on top of the POL-RD-02 figure, and POL-RD-09(1)'s anti-double-count rule is satisfied. No billing-integrity referral arises, and no driver compensation is due: the billed distance of 23.2 km against the traced 23.22 km is a shortfall of 0.02 km, far below the 1.0 km that POL-RD-04's compensation limb requires.

CONFIDENCE AND ESCALATION. Every fact the ruling rests on — the excess and its percentage, the optimal distance and duration, and the fare arithmetic — is carried by artifacts at weight_multiplier 1.0 (EV-GPS-02833, EV-TRIP-02833, EV-FARE-02833), so confidence is not capped and the MISSING advisory, which carries no deciding fact, does not lower it. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trip identifiers match across all three artifacts, the timestamps are consistent and run forward, the trace is not impaired, no cited artifact is missing in support of an invoked exculpatory clause, the refund is far below SGD 150.00 and below charged_total, and no fare line lacks a counterpart. The rider receives a partial refund of SGD 5.15; the balance of SGD 25.31 of the fare stands and no compensation is payable to the driver. Because the monetary effect of SGD 5.15 does not exceed the SGD 8.00 execution threshold in POL-GEN-05, the refund may be executed automatically, subject to the appeal route under POL-GEN-04.

ruling.explanation: Rider: your route-deviation claim is upheld in part, and the driver's 'Traffic.' explanation fails. POL-RD-01 makes the GPS trace the governing measurement, and EV-GPS-02833 records 23.22 km driven between the recorded pickup (14:53:35) and the recorded dropoff (15:23:45) against the booking-time optimal of 18.4 km on EV-TRIP-02833. That is 4.82 km of excess, 26.20% of optimal, passing both limbs of the establishment gate (over 0.8 km and over 20%). The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 182 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 s, so none of POL-RD-07(a)-(c) fires and no corroboration requirement or POL-RD-10(3) escalation follows. Your demand for a full refund is not supported: 26.20% is well short of the 50% (or 8.0 km) that POL-RD-01 makes a MATERIAL deviation, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged on this trip, its POL-RD-06(b) uplift to FULL_REFUND is unavailable, and the driver's profile confirms no pattern in any event (deviation_flags_90d 0 against 260 completed trips in 90 days), so no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises. The 'six deviation flags' figure in your filing is the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags; POL-GEN-01 makes it context only and POL-RD-06 tests the trailing-90-day field, so it is not a ground of decision. Your own profile adds no hurdle either: deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the POL-RD-08 threshold of 4, so no extra corroboration is required. The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02 on the METERED fare (EV-FARE-02833): recomputed fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 18.4 km = 13.80 distance + 0.28 x 24.8 min = 6.944 time) x the 1.0 surge multiplier recorded on the fare breakdown, + 0.80 platform fee, + 0.00 ERP/tolls = SGD 25.344. Charged total was SGD 30.46, so the refund is 30.46 - 25.344 = 5.116, rounded UP to SGD 5.15. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and only 16.80% of the charged total, far below the 90% that would substitute a full refund — so SGD 5.15, not the SGD 7.50 pleaded. Nothing is added on top: the fare carries no ERP or toll line, no airport surcharge (the trip ends at, and does not originate at, an airport), no waiting-time fee and no promo discount, and POL-RD-09(1) forbids counting any pass-through line twice. Driver: your sole explanation, 'Traffic.', carries no weight. The bundle holds no traffic advisory for this trip — EV-ADVIS-02833-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT — so POL-RD-03 cannot be run, and under POL-RD-13 and POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence ID neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies an amended optimal route. Because you named no advisory identifier, that absence is not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact under POL-RD-10(5), so the case is decided on the trace as measured rather than escalated. No driver compensation is payable: EV-CHAT-02833 is empty (no rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04), and the distance billed on the fare breakdown (23.2 km) is not more than 1.0 km short of the trace (23.22 km). The monetary effect of SGD 5.15 is at or below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically on issue; either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04.

discards.claim: The driver's uncited traffic assertion is not an escalation trigger, so the case can and should be decided with money moving. EV-ADVIS-02833-01 is named by no party in support of the excuse; the counterparty statement 'Traffic.' cites no evidence id at all. Under POL-RD-13(1) an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact within POL-RD-10(5) — the absence of an artifact no party has cited is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction in it. Every other POL-RD-10 trigger is absent too: trip identifiers match across the three artifacts, no pickup or dropoff timestamps disagree, the trace is not impaired, and the refund is well under SGD 150.00 and under charged_total. The rider should therefore receive a monetary partial refund rather than having the amount held on an escalation.
